Reshape Replicate Simulation Output for Covariate Forest Plots

Source: R/df_forest_preprocess.R
df_forest_preprocess.Rd

Turns raw replicate simulation output into the long draws frame df_forest() consumes. Input is one row per covariate scenario per replicate with the exposure metrics as columns (an N replicates by M scenarios table, the shape an mrgsolve forest simulation produces once metrics are derived over the interval of interest). Output is one row per metric per scenario per replicate, with the covariate name and the covariate level label.

Scenarios are read from the covariate columns themselves: the reference scenario is the one where every covariate equals its cov_val_ref value, and every other scenario must differ from it in exactly one covariate, which becomes that scenario's covariate name. No scenario identifier column is needed.

Usage

df_forest_preprocess(
  data,
  metric_vars,
  cov_vars,
  cov_val_ref,
  irep_name = "SIM",
  ratio = TRUE,
  ratio_suffix = "RATIO",
  cov_labels = NULL,
  cov_name_ref = "Reference",
  metric_name_var = "metric",
  metric_value_var = "value",
  cov_name_var = "cov_name",
  cov_level_var = "cov_level"
)

Arguments

data

Input data.frame. One row per covariate scenario per replicate, with exposure metrics as columns.

metric_vars

Character vector naming the exposure metric columns in data (e.g. c("CMAX", "AUC")). Must be numeric columns.

cov_vars

Character vector naming the covariate columns in data that define the scenarios (e.g. c("FOOD", "WTBL")).

cov_val_ref

Named vector giving the reference-scenario value of every cov_vars column (e.g. c(FOOD = 0, WTBL = 70)). Not to be confused with cov_level_ref in df_forest(), which holds display labels rather than source values.

irep_name

Column in data identifying the replicate. Accepts bare names or strings. Default is SIM. Required only when ratio = TRUE, which forms ratios within a replicate.

ratio

Logical. When TRUE (default), append a test/reference ratio metric for every entry of metric_vars. When FALSE, emit the absolute metrics only.

ratio_suffix

Suffix appended to a metric name to name its ratio. Default "RATIO", so AUC yields AUCRATIO.

cov_labels

Optional named list of display labels, one entry per covariate. Each entry is either a named character vector keyed on the character form of the covariate value (c("0" = "Fasted", "1" = "Fed")) or a function applied to the covariate values (function(x) paste(x, "kg")). Values with no label fall back to their character form with a warning. Default NULL (every level labeled by its character form).

cov_name_ref

Label written into the covariate name and covariate level columns for reference-scenario rows. Default "Reference", matching the df_forest() argument of the same name.

metric_name_var

Name of the output column of metric names. Accepts bare names or strings. Default metric.

metric_value_var

Name of the output column of metric values. Accepts bare names or strings. Default value.

cov_name_var

Name of the output column of covariate names. Accepts bare names or strings. Default cov_name.

cov_level_var

Name of the output column of covariate level labels. Accepts bare names or strings. Default cov_level.

Value

A data.frame with one row per metric per scenario per replicate, carrying a "cov_level_ref" attribute: a named character vector mapping each covariate that varies in data to its reference level label, ready to pass to df_forest() as cov_level_ref.

Details

Covariate values are matched to cov_val_ref on their character representation, so a numeric column and a character reference value still match. Covariate columns may not contain NA.

With ratio = TRUE each metric is also divided by the same replicate's reference-scenario value, producing a within-replicate test/reference ratio named <metric><ratio_suffix>. Because the parameter draw is shared across scenarios within a replicate, uncertainty common to both arms cancels in the ratio, which is why ratio intervals are narrower than absolute-exposure intervals.

Reference rows carry cov_name_ref as both their covariate name and their covariate level, so df_forest() renders them as the reference panel by default. To place the reference inside each covariate panel instead, pass the per-covariate reference labels to df_forest() as cov_level_ref; the mapping is returned on the "cov_level_ref" attribute of the output. Pass it explicitly; df_forest() does not read it.

Output columns

Every column of data that is not a metric column passes through unchanged and in its original order, followed by metric_name_var, metric_value_var, cov_name_var, and cov_level_var. An output name that collides with a passthrough column replaces it, with a warning.

See also

Other forest plot: df_forest(), is_forest_stats(), plot_build_forest(), plot_forest(), style_forest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_pmxforest(), style_forest_pumas()

Examples

# Raw replicate simulation output: one row per scenario per replicate
head(data_sad_pkforest_sim)
#>   ID SIM WTBL FOOD DOSE     CMAX     CMIN      AUC     CAVG
#> 1  1   1   70    0  200 844.8669 200.0502 12006.29 500.2621
#> 2  1   2   70    0  200 822.4267 272.0832 13463.48 560.9784
#> 3  1   3   70    0  200 868.3378 258.2627 13488.21 562.0089
#> 4  1   4   70    0  200 773.0414 157.6926 10383.56 432.6482
#> 5  1   5   70    0  200 913.1536 181.3835 12138.47 505.7697
#> 6  1   6   70    0  200 612.5367 213.1723 10439.84 434.9935

draws <- df_forest_preprocess(
  data_sad_pkforest_sim,
  metric_vars   = c("CMAX", "AUC"),
  cov_vars      = c("FOOD", "WTBL"),
  cov_val_ref = c(FOOD = 0, WTBL = 70),
  cov_labels    = list(
    FOOD = c("0" = "Fasted", "1" = "Fed"),
    WTBL = function(x) paste(x, "kg")
  )
)
head(draws)
#>   ID SIM WTBL FOOD DOSE     CMIN     CAVG    metric      value  cov_name
#> 1  1   1   70    0  200 200.0502 500.2621      CMAX   844.8669 Reference
#> 2  1   1   70    0  200 200.0502 500.2621       AUC 12006.2897 Reference
#> 3  1   1   70    0  200 200.0502 500.2621 CMAXRATIO     1.0000 Reference
#> 4  1   1   70    0  200 200.0502 500.2621  AUCRATIO     1.0000 Reference
#> 5  1   2   70    0  200 272.0832 560.9784      CMAX   822.4267 Reference
#> 6  1   2   70    0  200 272.0832 560.9784       AUC 13463.4824 Reference
#>   cov_level
#> 1 Reference
#> 2 Reference
#> 3 Reference
#> 4 Reference
#> 5 Reference
#> 6 Reference

# The per-covariate reference labels come back as an attribute
attr(draws, "cov_level_ref")
#>     FOOD     WTBL 
#> "Fasted"  "70 kg" 

# Feed straight into the forest pipeline
df_forest(draws)
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 24 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Reference, cov_level_ref = NULL
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>   metric  cov_name cov_level       est        lo       hi   n est_label
#> 1   CMAX Reference Reference  861.3751  741.2410 1005.205 500       861
#> 2   CMAX      FOOD       Fed 1465.1054 1180.1763 1830.221 500      1465
#> 3   CMAX      WTBL     50 kg 1118.5361  936.4438 1306.034 500      1119
#>   lo_label hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1      741     1005   861 (741, 1005)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2     1180     1830 1465 (1180, 1830)  FALSE         both
#> 3      936     1306  1119 (936, 1306)  FALSE         both
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.

# ... or draw the reference row in each covariate panel
df_forest(draws, cov_level_ref = attr(draws, "cov_level_ref"))
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 32 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Reference, cov_level_ref = c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg")
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>   metric  cov_name cov_level       est       lo       hi   n est_label lo_label
#> 1   CMAX Reference Reference  861.3751  741.241 1005.205 500       861      741
#> 2   CMAX      FOOD    Fasted  861.3751  741.241 1005.205 500       861      741
#> 3   CMAX      FOOD       Fed 1465.1054 1180.176 1830.221 500      1465     1180
#>   hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1     1005   861 (741, 1005)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2     1005   861 (741, 1005)   TRUE  distributed
#> 3     1830 1465 (1180, 1830)  FALSE         both
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.

# Absolute metrics only
df_forest_preprocess(
  data_sad_pkforest_sim,
  metric_vars   = "AUC",
  cov_vars      = c("FOOD", "WTBL"),
  cov_val_ref = c(FOOD = 0, WTBL = 70),
  ratio         = FALSE
)
